spec.name: Transatlantic Four-Seat Tourer
spec.raw_description: Four-seat tourer, London to New York non-stop, 5,570 km range, 45 min reserve, cruise 115 kt, stall under 55 kt.

defaulted_fields.taper_ratio: Assumed 0.45, near-elliptical lift for an unswept wing (Raymer 2ed, Ch. 4 (p. 56))
defaulted_fields.thickness_to_chord: Assumed 0.15 root aerofoil thickness (Raymer 2ed, Fig. 4.14 (p. 47): value read from chart trend, not a printed number)
defaulted_fields.ld_max: Assumed 11, typical fixed-gear GA (Raymer 2ed, Fig. 3.6 (p. 22): value estimated from chart, not a printed number)
defaulted_fields.bsfc_kg_per_j: Assumed 6.8e-8 kg/J (0.40 lb/hp/h) piston cruise SFC
defaulted_fields.limit_load_factor: Assumed +3.8 g limit, CS-23 normal category

infeasible_reason: The spiral closes at MTOW 3,467 kg, above the 2,722 kg limit for a single-engine piston aircraft (FAA AC 23.1309-1E, Class I (single reciprocating engine, under 6,000 lb)). The statistical methods don't apply that far out.

proposed_relaxation.reasoning: Flying 5,570 km non-stop requires a 40.9% fuel fraction, which drives up structural mass—pushing the wing spar from 151.7 kg to 157.8 kg across the design laps—until the aircraft converges at 3,467 kg, exceeding the 2,722 kg single-engine piston class limit. Because your description names a specific route from London to New York, preserving the full range is the primary requirement, while "four-seat tourer" only describes the general aircraft class. I therefore recommend reducing the cabin load to fly with 1 passenger instead of 3, which allows the design spiral to close at an MTOW of 2,422 kg while still crossing the Atlantic non-stop. Alternatively, if keeping all four seats is more important than the non-stop crossing, you can cut the range to 4,670 km to close the design at 2,719 kg.
